newsitem.title: BELGIUM: FOCUS-Virgin Express to raise bid for Air Liberte.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Virgin Express to raise bid for Air Liberte.

text.p: Richard Branson's Virgin Express regional airline will raise its planned bid for ailing French carrier Air Liberte to challenge an offer by rival British Airways Plc (BA), Virgin Express's chief executive officer Jonathan Ornstein said on Thursday.
When asked by Reuters whether Virgin Express would raise its bid he said "absolutely."
He declined to give any figures for the bid, which still had to be submitted. "We're still formulating a plan...(we still have) a couple of days," he said by telephone.
"I know it is getting a little late," he added.
"I talked to our colleagues in France and we're beginning to formulate a strategy," he said.

In Paris the court-appointed administrator of Air Liberte said he had not received any offers from Virgin Express to counter a 780 million French franc ($151.8 million) bid by British Airways and bank Rivaud.
Ornstein said earlier this month that investment bank Merrill Lynch and a French advisor were assisting Virgin Express in its bid.
BA became the leading contender in the race to scoop up Air Liberte when Rivaud, a founding shareholder of the French carrier, joined its bid on Wednesday.
"(BA's position) has become very strong," Ornstein said. "But in a way it has helped us. It becomes more interesting for us to become involved," he said.
BA has said it would make a 440 million French franc ($85.3 million) equity investment for a 70 percent stake in Air Liberte and Rivaud would put up 190 million for the remaining 30 percent.
On top of that Rivaud would make a write down on 500 million francs of its old stake and also on some 60 million francs in loan stocks.
Both companies will pay the costs of running Air Liberte during administration, estimated at 150 million francs.
The BA/Rivaud plan would safeguard 1,250 out of 1,400 Air Liberte jobs and aims for break-even in 1999.
Brussels-based Virgin Express, launched in April after Branson bought 90 percent of EuroBelgian Airlines (EBA), currently operates 14 Boeing 737 planes.
It expects to make a profit of over $10 million this year on turnover of $200 million and wants to more than double the number of its planes by the turn of the century.

Air Liberte owns about a quarter of the landing and take-off slots at Orly, Paris' second-largest airport. It lost 650 million francs in the first nine months of 1996 and has 1.5 billion francs of debt. ($ = 5.14 French Francs)
